channel.title: Typography Gems
channel.description: Free typography watch: typefaces, foundries and tools.

item.title: Crooli Sans — a friendlier Geist
item.description: A Geist fork: single-storey a, round dots, simpler R and G, with no redrawing or spacing changes. Variable wght 100 to 900 with italics, Latin, Vietnamese and Cyrillic. A good UI pick. OFL 1.1; brand-new project, published 28 October.

item.title: Qu Black 1.3.0
item.description: Bilingual Chinese-Latin family for code: Mono on a strict 2:1 grid (one hanzi = two ASCII cells), proportional Sans for UI and web, static and variable files. Fonts under OFL 1.1; version 1.3.0 from 24 October, a young project.

item.title: The Mother of All Fonts 4.3
item.description: Fonts traced from the title cards of Engelbart’s 1968 demo: AllCaps, SmallCaps and Humanist, proportional, Mono for terminals and a Text cut for small sizes, plus 237 emoji. No Greek or Cyrillic. OFL 1.1; version 4.3, 25 October.

item.title: BRANDSWOT Modular 2.100
item.description: Pixel display face on a 5 × 7 grid where every pixel is laid in brickwork; weight changes the mortar, not the shape. 7 weights, italics, variable wght 300 to 900, extended Latin, CDN and npm. OFL 1.1; v2.100 from 27 October.

item.title: Carry 1.1.0 — a font that does arithmetic
item.description: Type 128+256= and the font draws 384: addition, subtraction, multiplication and integer division, with no code, only OpenType substitutions (calt). A striking demo of what fonts can do. MIT license; v1.1.0 from 25 October.

item.title: Medeo — Sans, Mono and Pixel
item.description: Latin and Cyrillic family by DNF: variable Sans (weight 100 to 900, opsz axis 14 to 32 for text and headings), Mono for code, Pixel in five dot shapes. Italics, static fonts, npm package. OFL 1.1; release candidate RC4, published 27 October.

item.title: CADR Mono 1.1.0
item.description: Terminal monospace generated in Common Lisp, with no drawing tool: 935 glyphs, Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, box drawing, braille and Powerline computed from the cell. A lighter Dark grade for dark backgrounds, same metrics. OFL 1.1; young project, v1.1.0 from 15 October.

item.title: Static to Variable 0.6.2
item.description: Command-line tool that turns a folder of static weights into a single variable font: init, build, then release as TTF and WOFF2, plus split to go back. Needs Node, Python and uv. MIT license; v0.6.2, young but active project.

item.title: Limn Sans 1.002
item.description: Rounded sans derived from Quicksand, with pin-shaped dots, nine static weights from Thin to Black, ready-made WOFF2 and CSS for the web, and alternates (ss01, slashed zero). English and symbols only. OFL 1.1; stable release published 22 October.

item.title: Sleet Mono 1.00
item.description: Hand-drawn, Comic-style coding monospace, reworked from Comic Shanns using JetBrains Mono's metrics as a reference. Nerd Font build, Homebrew cask. MIT license; very young: one style and 103 glyphs, public roadmap.

item.title: BRND ProType 1.1
item.description: Venezuelan neo-grotesque superfamily: 49 styles across Condensed, Normal, Extended and Mono, 7 weights, italics, and 3 variable fonts (weight 300 to 900, width 88 to 114.5). Version 1.1 adds ProDigit (LCD) and ProLed (5×7 dot matrix). OFL 1.1, released 25 October.

item.title: ZFontManager 0.8.1 — font manager
item.description: Tauri/Rust font manager for Linux, Windows and macOS: live previews, one-click activate and deactivate, tags, collections, side-by-side compare, specimen sheets, built-in Google Fonts browser. Everything stays local. GPL-3.0, a young project (v0.8.1 on 26 Oct).

item.title: Counterpunch — browser-based font editor
item.description: Editor for variable and complex-script fonts, no install needed: live compilation with HarfBuzz shaping, bidirectional text, in-place component editing. Opens Glyphs, UFO, Designspace, VFJ and SFD. GPL-3.0, free (paid AI add-on). Alpha: near-daily preview builds.

item.title: bited 0.3.0 — bitmap font editor
item.description: Pixel font editor (monochrome Unicode BDF) built with Godot: composable drawing tools, preview with test-text presets, generators, light and dark modes. Version 0.3.0 moves the bitmap core to Rust and reworks the preview. MIT, under active development since 2024.

item.title: Kibernetyk Mono 1.0.1
item.description: Geometric monospace inspired by the Ukrainian Cybernetics School: 7 weights, Latin and Cyrillic, and since 1.0 the 128 box-drawing characters plus block elements, handy in terminals and TUIs. OFL 1.1, a young project (v1.0 on 18 October).

item.title: Shift 0.1.1 — éditeur de fontes multiplateforme
item.description: Font editor in Rust and TypeScript for macOS, Windows and Linux: outline drawing, variable fonts (axes, sources, instances), components, UFO, Designspace and Glyphs import, variable TrueType export. Kerning is planned. Apache 2.0, first alpha: work on copies.

item.title: FontYar 1.0 — gestionnaire de fontes local
item.description: Offline Tauri/Rust font manager (Windows, Linux, macOS): scans folders of TTF, OTF and WOFF2, flags duplicates, previews your own text, live weight slider for variable fonts, exports @font-face CSS or a ZIP. Interface built with Persian in mind. MIT, brand-new v1.0.

item.title: C64 Keyboard 1.112
item.description: Display font rebuilt from photos of Commodore 64 keycaps: capitals, f1 to f12 key labels and all 63 PETSCII graphics, with an online tester. Ideal for retro-computing visuals. Public domain (CC0), TTF, OTF and WOFF2, an October 2026 project.

item.title: LXGW Bright 26.10.22
item.description: A ready-made merge of the humanist Latin Ysabeau and the Chinese LXGW WenKai: an already balanced Latin-CJK pairing, in Simplified (GB) and Traditional (TC) editions. The 22 October release tracks WenKai 1.530. OFL 1.1, maintained since 2022.

item.title: FontGoggles 1.9.5
item.description: Free macOS viewer: drop in fonts (OTF, TTF, variable, UFO, designspace) to compare rendering, OpenType features and axes. 1.9.5 moves to HarfBuzz 14.6.0 and adds Cmd-R to reload every font. Apache 2.0, a mature tool since 2019.

item.title: Hyperglot 0.8.2
item.description: A database and tool (web, command line, Python) that tells you which languages a font really supports: 783 languages documented. Handy before picking a font for a multilingual project. 0.8.2 adds several Brazilian languages. Apache 2.0, active project.

item.title: FontFreeze — freeze a variable font
item.description: A web app that bakes an axis position and OpenType features (ligatures, alternates) into a new TTF or WOFF2 font. Useful for apps that only let you pick a family and a size. Everything runs in the browser. MIT, free, maintained since 2022.

item.title: Composite Font Studio
item.description: Builds a mixed CJK + Latin font the way InDesign composite fonts work: size, baseline and weight tuned per character class. Exports CSS or TTF/OTF/WOFF2, without uploading your files. MIT, free; a very young project (October 2026).

item.title: Gen Interface JP 0.8.1
item.description: A UI typeface blending Inter and Noto Sans JP so Latin and Japanese sit together, in two families (text and display) and eight weights, with subsetted webfonts on jsDelivr. 0.8.1 fixes per-weight baselines. Fonts under OFL, a 2026 project.

item.title: Nordwand Mono 1.3.4
item.description: A compact neo-grotesque monospace: the spirit of Univers in JetBrains Mono's proportions. Seven weights with italics, hexagonal zero and alternate glyphs, optional subtle ligatures, a Nerd Font build you compile yourself. MIT license, a 2026 project with frequent releases.

item.title: Ioskeley Mono 2.2
item.description: A coding font built on Iosevka, compact and geometric: ten weights, two widths, upright and italic. Three families (editor, terminal, no ligatures) and ready-made Nerd Font builds for VS Code, Zed, kitty or Ghostty. OFL 1.1, v2.2 released Oct 21, 2026.

item.title: Buena Mono 1.240
item.description: A variable monospace designed for writing as much as coding (Markdown, notes): weight axis 100-800 and slant 0 to -10°, 5,406 glyphs, 971 languages, coding ligatures. Derived from Fragment Mono. OFL 1.1, also on npm; a young project (Aug 2026), v1.240 out Oct 7.

item.title: Runebender — a font editor in Rust
item.description: A free font editor for UFO and designspace sources: outlines, spacing and kerning, variable fonts, OpenType feature code. Runs on macOS and Linux, built from source with Cargo. Apache 2.0, free. Experimental (v0.1), but under very active development.

item.title: Kerberos 1.4
item.description: A text serif in the Kis-Janson line, rare among free fonts: four variable axes (weight 300-700, optical size 8-72 pt, grade, lowercase height), small caps, ligatures, Latin, Greek and Cyrillic. For long reading on screen or in PDFs. OFL 1.1, a young project (Oct 2026).

item.title: Vavin 1.1
item.description: A Garamond for screens: derived from EB Garamond, with an x-height raised by 16% (0.72 of the cap height). Nine styles in three families, including a condensed and a display one, 503 Latin languages. Readable at small sizes, still classic. OFL 1.1, version 1.1 out Oct 2026.

item.title: Agràve Pro
item.description: A handwriting face designed for longer texts: open counters, even strokes, small caps and figure sets. Variable (weight 100-700), it was just merged into the Google Fonts repository. For a handwritten touch that stays readable. OFL 1.1, version 1.100, a 2026 project.

item.title: Punctum — a variable dot-matrix font
item.description: A 5x7 dot-matrix font with two axes: dot size (from pinhole LED to touching dots) and shape (round to square pixel). One continuous grid, real descenders, 108 ASCII characters plus arrows. Great for info boards, HUDs or retro posters. OFL 1.1, version 1.000 (Oct 2026).

item.title: Furifont 0.6
item.description: A Japanese font that shows furigana above kanji by itself, with no ruby markup or JavaScript, using ligatures. Derived from Source Han Sans and Serif, with a variable version and a CLI to build your own variant. Fonts OFL 1.1, code MIT; a young project (0.6.2, Oct 2026).

item.title: Clarity City
item.description: A geometric sans born at VMware for its Clarity design system, now on Google Fonts (Sep 2026) as a variable font: weights 100 to 900 with italics. A sober interface face for mockups, tools or a website. OFL 1.1, a proven font since 2019.

item.title: Libre Caslon Condensed
item.description: A narrow Caslon derived from Libre Caslon Text, now on Google Fonts: a variable condensed serif (400 to 700) with italics, rare among free fonts. Ideal for elegant headlines that fit on one line, posters or covers. OFL 1.1, maintained since 2023.

item.title: Kripa
item.description: A geometric sans for Latin and Devanagari sharing one rhythm: variable from 100 to 900, 20 character variants, discretionary ligatures, tabular figures. Handy for a bilingual identity or warm headlines. OFL 1.1, brand new, added to Google Fonts in September.

item.title: Isometra
item.description: A bold slab serif built loosely on a 60-degree isometric grid, in a single weight. For an eye used to 3D, display type that looks modeled: signage, logos, titles. OFL 1.1, a recent project (2025) added to Google Fonts in September 2026.

item.title: Fontaine 1.0.2
item.description: A JavaScript tool that generates fallback fonts matched to your web font's metrics, so the layout doesn't jump while it loads. 1.0.2 (Oct 21) adds metric-compatible Liberation fallbacks and better matching of local fonts. MIT, a mature unjs project.

item.title: Capsize
item.description: A web tool and CSS library that trim the empty space above and below text using the font's metrics, so headings finally sit exactly on the grid. The Oct 15 metrics update covers the October Google Fonts additions. MIT, stable since 2020.

item.title: Lilex 2.630
item.description: A coding font derived from IBM Plex Mono, with ligatures and a variable version. 2.630 (Oct 5) adds ASCII control pictures, an overline, rounded commas and quotes (ss05), and fixes ligature and diacritic alignment. OFL 1.1, active since 2019.

item.title: Sarasa Gothic 1.0.42
item.description: A composite font combining Inter, Iosevka and Source Han Sans: Latin plus Chinese, Japanese and Korean that line up, including monospaced variants for terminals and code. Version 1.0.42 (Sep 26), as TTF, TTC or SuperTTC. OFL 1.1, mature and widely used.

item.title: Noto Emoji — Unicode 18
item.description: Google's open emoji library moves to Unicode 18 (Sep 24): 2D color font v2.057, a 3D edition v3.054 shipped separately, plus the source SVGs and PNGs. A variable monochrome version is also on Google Fonts. Fonts under OFL 1.1, tools under Apache 2.0.

item.title: HarfBuzz 14.6.0
item.description: The text-shaping engine behind Chrome, Firefox, Android and LibreOffice. 14.6.0 (Oct 5) fixes a regression with out-of-range glyph IDs, and adds the DMAP table and FeatureVariations 1.1 lookup variations. "Old MIT" license, an industry reference.

item.title: glyphsLib 6.16
item.description: The Python bridge that converts .glyphs sources to UFO and designspace, so you can build with fontmake without opening Glyphs. 6.16 (Oct 8) places corner components like Glyphs 3.5, and 6.16.1 (Oct 16) refines instances and alignment zones. Apache 2.0, mature.

item.title: Google Sans Flex 5.000
item.description: Google's brand typeface, released as open source: a geometric variable sans on five axes (weight 1–1000, width 25–151, slant, ROND roundness, optical sizes 1–144). 5.000 (Oct 9) drops the GRAD axis and refines tiny sizes. OFL 1.1, merged into the google/fonts repo.

item.title: Tiny5 and Tiny5 Duo 2.007 — pixel type goes variable
item.description: A 5-pixel-tall pixel font, now variable: weight, width, roundness and two rare axes, BLED (ink spread, CRT glow) and JITT (jitter), plus italics. Tiny5 Duo uses 2-pixel stems. Great for HUDs and retro interfaces. OFL, merged into google/fonts on Oct 9.

item.title: Firjar — a bilingual Kufic Arabic-Latin typeface
item.description: A Kufic-inspired sans built like a compass drawing (quarter circles and clean straight lines), pairing Arabic and Latin in one variable family: weight 100–800, width 75–125. For headlines, branding and bilingual UI. By Mestara Type, OFL, added to google/fonts on Oct 15.

item.title: Fontspector 1.9
item.description: Fontbakery's successor, rewritten in Rust: font quality checks from the command line, as a Python module or right in the browser (WASM), with Google Fonts, OpenType and universal profiles. 1.9 (Oct 9) can fix some issues directly in UFO sources. Apache 2.0.

item.title: LXGW WenKai 1.530
item.description: A free Chinese kai-style font derived from Fontworks' Klee One, popular for reading. 1.530 (Oct 17) adds 50 Unicode 18 small seal script characters, mahjong and dice symbols, completes JIS X 0213 kanji and redraws hundreds of glyphs. OFL 1.1.

item.title: Cal Sans 2.011
item.description: Cal.com's geometric sans, now a variable system: weight 400–700, optical sizes 8–45 pt, a GEOM axis (from A11y to Geo), real italics. 2.011 (Oct 15) adds Cal Sans Phlex, morphing letterforms without avar2. OFL 1.1; Flex is still experimental.

item.title: Kode Mono 2.003
item.description: A coding monospace with ligatures and Powerline glyphs. The 2.0 series adds two variable axes, width (75–125) and roundness (ROND 0–100), plus an ss01 set that tells D/0/O and 8/B apart. 2.003 (Oct 8) is heading to Google Fonts. OFL 1.1, mature since 2023.

item.title: Wavefont and Linefont — charts written as text
item.description: Two variable fonts by Dmitry Iv.: each character becomes a bar (Wavefont: waveforms, histograms) or a curve point (Linefont: time series). Great for tiny charts in a web UI without canvas. Updated on Google Fonts on Oct 9. OFL 1.1.

item.title: Libron 0.31
item.description: A reading serif derived from Readerly (itself based on Newsreader), hand-edited in FontForge for a calmer texture. Ready-made builds for Kobo, KOReader, Kindle, desktop and web. 0.31 (Oct 9) adds fractions, superscripts and Unicode spaces. OFL, in active development.

item.title: Ark Pixel Font 2026.10.16
item.description: An open source pixel font in 10 and 12 px, covering Latin and Chinese/Japanese/Korean, in monospaced or proportional versions with kerning. Perfect for a game UI or a retro HUD. Released Oct 16 (16 px dropped). Fonts OFL 1.1, code MIT, active since 2021.

item.title: Redaction — the legal-document serif, coming to Google Fonts
item.description: Serif by Jeremy Mickel (MCKL), between Times and Century Schoolbook, in 7 families: one clean and six increasingly "photocopied" (10 to 100). Great for textured titles or an archival look. OFL 1.1, Google Fonts onboarding under way (Oct 2026).

item.title: Fontra Pak 2026.10
item.description: The free font editor that runs in your browser, bundled for macOS, Windows and Linux. 2026.10 (Oct 5) adds a proper File menu and a button to open a .ufo or .fontra project directly. GPL 3.0, still in active development, monthly releases.

item.title: Glyphr Studio 2.10.6
item.description: A 100% web-based font editor, no install or account, built for beginners: draw a display alphabet or an icon font in one evening. 2.10.6 (Oct 2, 2026) fixes tool states and search within a Unicode range. GPL 3.0, free.

item.title: Iosevka 34.9
item.description: A narrow, fully configurable monospace (glyph variants, custom builds), available as Term, Slab, Aile and Etoile. 34.9 (Sept 26, 2026) adds variants for ζ, ξ, ς and dozens of diacritics. OFL 1.1, a very mature project since 2015.

item.title: IBM Plex Mono variable
item.description: Plex Mono is finally a variable font: one file, weight axis from 100 to 700, Thin to Bold instances. Handy for code and web UI without juggling files. Joins Plex Serif and Sans variable. OFL 1.1, a very mature IBM family.

item.title: fontc 1.0 — Google's font compiler in Rust
item.description: Stable release (Sept 1, 2026) of Google Fonts' Rust compiler, a drop-in replacement for fontmake for Glyphs or UFO sources: variable fonts compiled much faster. TrueType only, no static instances. Apache 2.0, tested on ~3,450 targets.

item.title: fontTools 4.67
item.description: The Python Swiss Army knife for fonts (ttx, subset, varLib) at 4.67 (Oct 14, 2026): instancing of COLRv1 variable fonts, feaLib and CFF2 fixes. For slimming a web font, freezing an axis or scripting a pipeline. MIT, very mature.

item.title: Geist 1.8.1
item.description: Vercel's Geist Sans and Geist Mono, understated, for UI and code. 1.8.1 (Oct 16, 2026) aligns binary versions with the package and fixes the lowercase omega, which pointed to the Ohm sign. OFL 1.1, regular releases since 2023.

item.title: Monaspace 1.4
item.description: GitHub Next's monospace superfamily (Neon, Argon, Xenon, Radon, Krypton) with “texture healing” that balances wide and narrow letters. 1.400 adds Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese and IPA. Variable, web and Nerd Fonts. OFL 1.1.

item.title: Maple Mono 7.9
item.description: Rounded monospace for IDEs and terminals: ligatures, Nerd Font icons, a script to freeze your variants (a “Normal” option close to JetBrains Mono). 7.9 adds IPA glyphs and fixes feature freezing. OFL 1.1, ~29,000 stars.

item.title: Fontsource
item.description: Thousands of free fonts as npm packages to self-host: one import and the font, static or variable, is served by your own site, with no third-party CDN. Online catalog for testing. MIT code, each font keeps its own licence (often OFL).

item.title: Collletttivo — Italian libre foundry
item.description: Italian collective whose whole catalog is under the SIL OFL: Apfel Grotezk, Ronzino, Sprat (18 weights + variable), Halibut, Necto Mono… Expressive display faces usable commercially and in renders, with credit requested.

item.title: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next
item.description: 2024 version of the Braille Institute's hyperlegible typeface: new glyphs, revised kerning, 6 weights with italics (versus 2). OFL 1.1, sources on GitHub, on Google Fonts. Ideal for UI, subtitles and docs.

item.title: Inter 4.1
item.description: The reference screen sans-serif (OFL 1.1), variable with an optical size axis and many OpenType features (tabular figures, alternates). A mature project; latest version 4.1 (Nov 2024). A safe choice for interfaces and pairing.

item.title: FontForge 20251009
item.description: Free and open source font editor (Windows, macOS, Linux), scriptable in Python: draw, retouch and convert your own fonts. A mature project; latest version released Oct 9, 2025. Free (donations).
